description: Canonical Taste Test attribute library, transcribed from 'Taste Test attributes' (Marketeers). This file is the source of truth: backend/scripts/seed_taste_test_library.py upserts it into the taste_test_questions collection. Previously the library existed only inside an untracked Taste_Test_restructured.xlsx, so it could not be rebuilt or reviewed.

notes.scales: Sensory sub-attributes use a 5-point CENTERED scale: every point carries its own label and the MIDDLE label is the ideal answer ('مناسب' = suitable for me). 'Overall ...' questions use a 1-10 HEDONIC scale where 10 is best. Purchase intent (T81) is a 5-point MONOTONIC ladder where 5 is best - it looks like a centered scale but is not one, so its labels say so explicitly.
notes.interpretation: There is deliberately no separate 'JAR' flag. The point labels ARE the semantics - reporting and AI read point_labels_ar / point_labels_en to decide whether the midpoint or the top of a scale is the good outcome.
notes.status: question_status is the platform's inclusion rule, not research guidance. 'fixed' questions are asked in every taste test; 'optional' questions are asked only when their main attribute is selected during survey creation. An 'Overall ...' row has no sub-attribute, so it is pulled in automatically whenever its main attribute is chosen. Separately, condition_ar/condition_en carry the source document's advice that an attribute (acidity, bitterness, crispness) is only worth measuring when that characteristic is natural and expected in the product.

instructions.centered_en: (Pick the answer that suits you best - the middle option means it is exactly right for you)
